newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up on Wednesday on improved market sentiment helped by rises on the Dalian Commodity Exchange, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,340 yuan ($402) per tonne, rising 16 yuan. It opened at 3,330 yuan and hit a low of 3,325 yuan.
March did not trade, May rose 129 yuan to 3,210, July 60 to 3,315, November 20 to 3,350 and the January 1998 contract 20 to 3,360.
Combined volume rose to 24,700 tonnes from 22,700.
Soybeans opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said continued rises in soybean contract prices on the Dalian Commodity Exchange have improved confidence of long position holders in Shanghai.
"But volume did not grow very much, indicating institutional investors are still staying on the sidelines," one trader said.
A floor source said demand for spot soybeans in China's northeast has increased lately and this had been reflected in the gains on the futures market. ($1=8.2955 yuan)
